note: Apps the tool can fetch and sideload, so nobody has to go hunting for an APK. Only two kinds of source are allowed: the official F-Droid repo, and a project's own GitHub releases. No mirrors, no APKPure, no 'APK download' sites — those are the exact places that serve repackaged binaries, and on some ISPs they are DNS-blocked anyway. Everything here is open source.

apps.name: F-Droid
apps.blurb: The store everything else here comes from. Install it so the person can update these apps themselves afterwards.

apps.name: Aurora Store
apps.blurb: An anonymous front end for Google Play. Useful if you disabled the Play Store but still need an app that only exists there.
apps.note: Taken from F-Droid: the old whyorean/AuroraStore GitHub releases are gone, the project moved to GitLab.

apps.name: Fossify Launcher
apps.blurb: A plain icon grid with no ads and no feed. Comfortable and familiar, but measured heavier than Samsung's own launcher, so pick it for the look rather than for the memory.

apps.name: Fossify Launcher (large tiles)
apps.blurb: Same app, configured for big icons and few of them. What Elder mode offers; chosen for legibility, not for memory.

apps.name: Olauncher
apps.blurb: Text-only home screen, no icons at all. Single page. Drastic and very calming.

apps.name: Kvaesitso
apps.blurb: Search-first launcher, the most polished of the open-source ones. Heavier than the others.

apps.name: KISS
apps.blurb: One screen: favourites along the bottom, a search bar, nothing to swipe. The lightest usable home screen we have measured, and still has widgets if you want them.

apps.name: µLauncher
apps.blurb: One page, no icons: swipe from the edges to apps you choose. A 4 MB APK that is surprisingly not the lightest at runtime.

apps.name: YAM Launcher
apps.blurb: A text list of apps and the time. Single page, almost as light as KISS, and simpler to live with if you dislike a search box.

apps.name: Lawnchair
apps.blurb: The closest open-source thing to Nova Launcher: icon grid, dock, app drawer, folders, gestures, icon packs, adjustable grid size. What to pick if you liked Nova and want the source open.
apps.note: Needs prerelease: Lawnchair only tags betas, so GitHub's 'latest release' is version 1.2 from 2020. The debug nightly is excluded by name; this takes the newest tagged beta.

apps.name: Neo Launcher
apps.blurb: A Lawnchair fork that goes further on customisation — closer to Nova's tweak-everything character, at the cost of more settings to wade through.

apps.name: Fossify Phone
apps.blurb: A dialer with large buttons and no caller-ID upload.

apps.name: Fossify Messages
apps.blurb: SMS without an ad-supported RCS layer on top.

apps.name: Fossify Gallery
apps.blurb: Shows the photos on the phone, with folders, an editor, favourites, a recycle bin and hidden folders. No cloud, no account, no ads. Measured 32 MB against Samsung Gallery's 43 MB.

apps.name: FUTO Keyboard
apps.blurb: A keyboard that does not send what you type anywhere. Install before disabling Gboard.

apps.name: Fennec (Firefox)
apps.blurb: Firefox built by F-Droid, with uBlock Origin available. Install before disabling Chrome.

apps.name: Organic Maps
apps.blurb: Offline maps and navigation. The practical replacement if you turn off Google Maps.

apps.name: Termux
apps.blurb: The Linux userland everything in the server section runs inside.
apps.note: From F-Droid on purpose. The Play Store build is abandoned, and the GitHub assets are debug-signed, so add-ons installed from anywhere else refuse to talk to them. Termux and its add-ons must all come from the same source.

apps.name: Termux:Boot
apps.blurb: Runs your service scripts when the phone restarts. Without it, a reboot ends your server.
apps.note: Signing key must match Termux, so this comes from F-Droid too.

apps.name: Termux:API
apps.blurb: Lets scripts read the battery, hold a wake lock and send notifications.

apps.name: Tailscale
apps.blurb: Reach the phone's services from anywhere without opening a port or touching the router.

apps.name: Shizuku
apps.blurb: Gives other apps ADB-level access without a computer. Not needed by this tool, handy next to it.

apps.name: Syncthing-Fork
apps.blurb: Keeps folders in sync with your other machines, peer to peer.
apps.note: The original com.nutomic.syncthingandroid was discontinued in 2024 and is gone from F-Droid. This maintained fork is the successor.

apps.name: KeePassDX
apps.blurb: Offline password manager.

apps.name: Aegis Authenticator
apps.blurb: Two-factor codes, exportable, unlike Google Authenticator.

apps.name: NewPipe
apps.blurb: YouTube without the app, the ads or the account. What to install if you disabled YouTube.

apps.name: VLC
apps.blurb: Plays the media files the OEM player was the only thing opening.

apps.name: PCAPdroid
apps.blurb: Shows what each app is actually talking to, with no root. Worth running before you decide what to disable.
